title: Isandro and the Will
premise: Odile Villalobos, a night dispatcher whose off-the-books investigations have quietly solved three 'accidental' deaths, is hired by a nervous stranger named Isandro to prove that his wealthy uncle will NOT be murdered at the family's anniversary dinner — a crime that, according to an anonymous letter, has already been planned in detail. As Odile infiltrates the Villalobos-adjacent household under cover as event staff, she discovers the letter was written by Isandro himself, who may be the killer rehearsing an alibi — or the only honest man in a family where the will, rewritten weeks ago, gives everyone a motive. The real architect of the plot turns out to be the family lawyer, who forged the new will and groomed Isandro as a patsy; Odile must expose him mid-toast at the dinner, trading her anonymity for justice and finding, in Isandro's stubborn decency, the first family she's ever chosen.
about_author: Gideon Oyelaran is a former court clerk from Ibadan who now writes mysteries from a small apartment above a laundromat in Lisbon. He claims his plots come from reading other people's discarded legal paperwork, which he insists he found legally.

chapters.title: The Night Frequency
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A slow shift at Despacho Taxi: radio chatter, a fare who never arrives, and a quiet flashback to the drowned fisherman whose 'accident' she unraveled last winter. Establishes her method — listening for what people don't say. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, the comfort of patterns.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A client called Isandro meets her at a diner, pays triple rate, and asks her to prove a murder will not happen at his uncle Aurelio's anniversary dinner in three weeks. He hands her an anonymous letter describing the murder in chilling detail. Beat: unease — she's never been hired to prevent a crime.

chapters.title: The Letter's Grammar
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She dissects the threat letter: its phrasing mirrors police report language no civilian would use. She cross-references it against her old case files and finds one phrase repeated verbatim from the fisherman case. Beat: cold recognition — whoever wrote this knows her work.

chapters.title: House of Aurelio
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He tours us through the family estate: Uncle Aurelio, fading but sharp; cousins Marisol and Teo circling the fortune; the lawyer Bautista Quintero presiding like a priest. Isandro watches everyone measure each other against the will. Beat: dread dressed as hospitality.

chapters.title: Catering Credentials
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Using forged references, she takes a job with the catering company hired for the dinner. First walkthrough of the house; she maps exits, notes a locked study, and catches Marisol burning papers in a garden brazier. Beat: the thrill of infiltration curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Signature
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She revisits her three solved deaths and realizes all three estates passed through Quintero's firm. The pattern she thought was coincidence now looks like a career. Beat: vertigo — she hasn't been hunting a killer; she's been walking beside one for years.

chapters.title: What Isandro Knows
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Odile confronts Isandro about the letter; he admits he wrote it after finding a draft of the new will naming him sole heir — a draft he says he never signed. Each suspects the other. Beat: mutual suspicion sharpening into reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Marisol's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Deep in debt, she calculates exactly what her share of the inheritance erases — and notices the new will's dates don't match Aurelio's hospital records. She keeps the discrepancy to herself. Beat: complicity; corruption beginning as self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Locked Study
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. During a staff day-off, she picks the study lock and photographs the will file: signatures dated during a week Aurelio was sedated post-surgery. Someone photographs HER through the window. Beat: triumph flipping instantly to exposure.

chapters.title: Teo's Confession That Isn't
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. Teo, the black-sheep cousin, drunkenly tells Odile he's being blackmailed over an old hit-and-run — by someone with access to sealed police files. He doesn't know who. Beat: pity; the family's rot predates the will.

chapters.title: Anniversary Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Full rehearsal dinner run-through. She times the toast, the service, the power cut during the storm drill. Quintero quizzes her too precisely about her employment history. Beat: the hunter realizing she is also prey.

chapters.title: The Fisherman's Widow
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She tracks down the widow from her first case, who reveals Quintero visited her offering to 'expedite' the settlement — right before she stopped asking questions. Beat: grief and fury braided together; the stakes turn personal.

chapters.title: Isandro's Alibi Problem
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He confesses to Odile that someone has been building a case against him: receipts, witnesses, a gun registered in his name. If Aurelio dies, Isandro hangs. Beat: terror — he hired her to save himself as much as his uncle.

chapters.title: Midnight Dispatch
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Back on shift, she uses the taxi network — drivers see everything — to reconstruct Quintero's movements for a month. Three late-night runs to the marina, the quarry, the underpass. Her three cases. Beat: grim certainty hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Marisol Sells Out
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Cornered by Odile with the date discrepancy, Marisol trades what she knows: Quintero drafted the new will before Aurelio's diagnosis, and someone paid her silence. Beat: betrayal acknowledged; even the corrupt want to be seen.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Another anonymous letter arrives — this one addressed to her by name, describing her own death at the dinner. It uses a phrase only Isandro knew she'd flagged. Has he turned? Or is he being framed twice? Beat: paranoia at full pitch.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Odile and Isandro lay everything bare — the letter, the alibi trap, the frame. They realize the second letter's phrase came from a conversation Quintero could have overheard via the house intercom system. Beat: trust finally earned through shared danger.

chapters.title: Dinner Service
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Anniversary night. Storm outside; she works the room with a tray and an earpiece, coordinating with Isandro while Aurelio rises to speak. The wine service begins. Beat: coiled stillness, every gesture loaded.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Quintero engineers a power cut; in the dark, the poisoned glass is swapped. But Odile switched the decanters an hour earlier, and Isandro publicly demands the will be read tonight. Quintero, certain his plan holds, raises his own glass first. Beat: the trap closing from both ends.

chapters.title: What the File Knew
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Lights return; Aurelio, warned and unharmed, watches as Odile lays out the forged dates, the blackmail trail, the three 'accidents,' and the intercom recordings. Quintero's composure cracks when she quotes his own report language back to him. Beat: cathartic exposure.

chapters.title: After the Glass
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Arrests; Marisol cooperates for leniency; Teo weeps with relief; Aurelio, humbled, tears up the contested will and asks Isandro to stay — not for money, but for family. Odile declines any reward. Beat: exhaustion and unexpected tenderness.

chapters.title: Open Line
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, epilogue. Weeks later, back on the night shift, she gets a call from a stranger whose sister's car went off a bridge. Isandro brings her coffee unasked — found family, quietly forming. She picks up the pen. Beat: hopeful resolve; the frequency stays open.
